text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Autoscaler failover triggered in us-west-2 — queue depth > 12k for gpu-serving pool, scale attempts failing with capacity errors. Probe ID: probe-8245

oncall-casey: paging in, I'm on it. seeing spike on dashboards, thanks bot.

sre-alex: grabbing logs, can everyone stop routing new heavy batch jobs to gpu pool? recommend flip traffic to ded-1 if possible.

runtime-jen: i see repeated CUDA/Xid errors in /var/log/nvidia-driver.log on nodes gpu-3, gpu-5 -> "Xid 31" pattern, plus oom-killer events. driver restarts seem to be happening every ~90s which confuses the autoscaler. stacktrace: `nvidia: nmm-client: gpu reset`

prod-eng-omar: tagging customers that might be impacted in #support. can we confirm which routes are failing? token-rate shows queue growth on /v1/generate and /v1/chat.

support-lara: getting initial customer-impact matrix. top 3 orgs with errors: acme-inc (high), beta-startup (medium), internal-monitoring (low). support ticket spike started ~5m ago. cc @prod-eng-omar

oncall-casey: running quick mitigation plan: 1) taint problematic nodes to stop scheduling, 2) force autoscaler cooldown to avoid noisy restarts, 3) route new requests to us-east fallback. Any objections?

runtime-jen: go for it. taint will help but autoscaler currently refuses new nodes because driver plugin reports nodes NotReady. autoscaler logs: `scaleUp failed: all candidate nodes have taints or plugin failed`

sre-alex: executing commands now:
```
# mark nodes unschedulable to stop new tasks
kubectl label node gpu-3 gpu-5 maintenance=true --overwrite
kubectl cordon gpu-3 gpu-5
# suggest temporary scale target reduction to reduce churn
kubectl patch hpa gpu-serving -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":2}}'
```

infra-bot: command accepted, node labels applied.

oncall-casey: i'm toggling routing rule to prefer us-east (canary) for new requests. leaving 5% to us-west for monitoring.

prod-eng-omar: set a short TTL on responses to avoid client retries compounding queue. also enable 503 short-circuit for long queue times.

support-lara: posting status update to customers: "We're investigating increased error rates for generation endpoints in us-west-2. Our team is rerouting traffic and performing node remediation. We'll update in 30 minutes or as we have new info." :thumbsup:

runtime-jen: looking at kernel logs, sees frequent "GPU reset pending" and `oom_reaper` events. suspect driver regression after last hotpatch. pattern: nodes started showing higher mem fragmentation -> cuda allocations failing -> Xid 31 -> driver reset -> kubelet marks container failed.

sre-alex: i've forced a graceful restart of nvidia-driver on gpu-3 and gpu-5 to stop the crash loop. command:
```
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-drivers.service || sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm && sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm
```

runtime-jen: seeing driver come back up, but pods are staying in CrashLoopBackOff due to OOM of downstream process. increasing container memory request temporarily might help but we need to avoid exhausting host memory.

oncall-casey: plan B: evacuate heavy pods from those nodes and reboot them. srep?

sre-alex: draining now (graceful eviction):
```
kubectl drain gpu-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60
kubectl drain gpu-5 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60
```

infra-bot: drain commands accepted, pods being rescheduled. autoscaler temporarily suppressed to avoid scaling on eviction noise.

prod-eng-omar: can we toggle fallback model variants (smaller quantized) to reduce memory pressure on live nodes? That would lower per-request GPU allocation.

runtime-jen: yes — switching route for non-critical traffic to the q4_1 variant now. will post config snippet.
```
routes:
  - match: "/v1/generate"
    weight:
      us-west: 0.05
      us-east: 0.95
    model_overrides:
      us-east: "gptx-q4_1"
```

support-lara: updating customers: "Traffic rerouted to alternate region, some requests may see model fallbacks. We're seeing reduced error rates for most tenants. ETA for full restoration: 35-50 minutes depending on node reboots."

oncall-casey: rebooting gpu-3 and gpu-5 now.

runtime-jen: note for postmortem: hotpatch v2026.02.11 applied to driver nodes last night could correlate. saving driver versions and dmesg outputs.

sre-alex: telemetry shows queue depth halved after reroute and taint. autoscaler no longer trying to create new nodes because plugin now gets stable node states. good sign.

incident-bot: UPDATE: Pager duty incident created PD-4217. Priority: P1. Linked runbook: gpu-exhaustion-autoscaler.

prod-eng-omar: customer-impact snapshot: approx 7% of total requests in us-west saw 5xx during peak window. no data exfiltration. SLA blips noted for 2 enterprise customers, currently triaged by accounts.

support-lara: raising follow-up action: notify affected customers with root-cause summary once we confirm driver regression. drafting email.

oncall-casey: nodes back up, pods stabilized, queue drained to normal levels. keeping autoscaler disabled for 10 more mins to observe.

runtime-jen: collecting logs and uploading to internal bucket for RCA. important artifacts:
- /var/log/nvidia-driver.log (Xid events)
- dmesg dump around resets
- kubelet and autoscaler logs for scale attempts
- snapshot of model memory alloc profiles

sre-alex: creating Jira follow-up for driver rollback plan and a safer autoscaler cooldown config to avoid thrash on transient driver flapping.

prod-eng-omar: good work. next steps: controlled revert of driver hotpatch in staging, run long mem-stress and allocation tests, update runbook with node taint playbook.

support-lara: posting final customer note after review.

oncall-casey: incident CLOSED (mitigated). leaving PD-4217 open for RCA until postmortem complete. :white_check_mark:

runtime-jen: postmortem owners: runtime-jen, sre-alex. target: 72h. include metric snapshots, driver binary hash, and decision log for autoscaler tune.

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: Mitigation executed: traffic reroute, node taint/cordon, driver restart, node reboots. Queue growth stopped, error rate returned to baseline.

sre-alex: final note — please follow up with infra team about possible kernel/driver combo that increases memory fragmentation under mixed workload. worth a preemptive test on ded-prod.

support-lara: thanks team. I'll update customers once RCA draft is ready. :pray:
